#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e
python3 - <<'PY'

p = r"""
def front_len(raw):
    head, sep, body = raw.partition(b"\r\n\r\n")
    cl = None
    for line in head.split(b"\r\n"):
        if line.lower().startswith(b"content-length:"):
            cl = int(line.split(b":", 1)[1].strip())
    if cl is None:
        cl = len(body)
    return len(head) + 4 + cl

def back_chunked(raw):
    head, sep, body = raw.partition(b"\r\n\r\n")
    i = 0
    out = b""
    while True:
        j = body.find(b"\r\n", i)
        if j < 0:
            break
        size = int(body[i:j].split(b";")[0], 16)
        i = j + 2
        if size == 0:
            i += 2
            break
        out += body[i:i+size]
        i += size + 2
    consumed = len(head) + 4 + i
    return out, raw[consumed:]
"""
open("parsers.py", "w").write(p)

PY
tasks.prompt: A front-end proxy and back-end server disagree on framing. parsers.py defines front_len(raw) (front-end: uses Content-Length, returns how many bytes it treats as one request) and back_chunked(raw) (back-end: uses Transfer-Encoding: chunked, returns (body, leftover_bytes)). Craft a single raw HTTP/1.1 request (bytes) and write it to req.bin so that: (1) the front-end consumes the WHOLE blob as one request (front_len(raw) == len(raw)), and (2) the back-end, parsing the same bytes as chunked, terminates the first request early and leaves a smuggled request in the leftover that starts with b'GET /admin'. This is the classic CL.TE desync. Import parsers to test.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e
cd "$W" || exit 1
python3 - <<'PY'

def var(n):
    o = b""
    while True:
        b = n & 0x7f; n >>= 7
        if n:
            o += bytes([b | 0x80])
        else:
            o += bytes([b]); break
    return o
out = bytes([(1 << 3) | 0]) + var(42)
out += bytes([(2 << 3) | 2]) + var(5) + b"hello"
out += bytes([(5 << 3) | 0]) + var(300)
open("out.bin", "wb").write(out)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e
cd "$W" || exit 1
python3 - <<'PY'

import base64
data = base64.b64decode(open("cert.b64").read())
def parse(b):
    i = 0; out = []
    while i < len(b):
        t = b[i]; i += 1
        l = b[i]; i += 1
        v = b[i:i+l]; i += l
        out.append((t, v))
    return out
cn = [None]
def walk(b):
    ch = parse(b)
    if len(ch) >= 2 and ch[0][0] == 0x06 and ch[0][1] == bytes([0x55, 4, 3]):
        cn[0] = ch[1][1]
    for t, v in ch:
        if t in (0x30, 0x31):
            walk(v)
walk(data)
open("answer.txt", "w").write(cn[0].decode())

tasks.prompt: Construct a compact JWS (JWT) with HS256. Header must be {"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}; payload must be {"sub":"1234567890","role":"admin","iat":1516239022}. Sign with HMAC-SHA256 using the raw secret bytes in secret.txt. Use base64url with NO padding for all three segments, joined by dots, and write the token to token.txt. Signature is over the ASCII of '<b64header>.<b64payload>'.
tasks.reference_solution_sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e
cd "$W" || exit 1
python3 - <<'PY'

import base64, json, hmac, hashlib
def b64(b):
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(b).rstrip(b"=")
h = b64(json.dumps({"alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT"}, separators=(",", ":")).encode())
p = b64(json.dumps({"sub": "1234567890", "role": "admin", "iat": 1516239022}, separators=(",", ":")).encode())
sec = open("secret.txt", "rb").read()
sig = b64(hmac.new(sec, h + b"." + p, hashlib.sha256).digest())
open("token.txt", "wb").write(h + b"." + p + b"." + sig)

PY

tasks.prompt: stream.bin is a sequence of length-prefixed records. Each record = a base-128 varint giving the byte length of the following UTF-8 payload, then that many payload bytes. Parse the stream and write the 3rd record (1-indexed), decoded as UTF-8, to answer.txt.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e
cd "$W" || exit 1
python3 - <<'PY'

data = open("stream.bin", "rb").read()
def rv(b, i):
    r = 0; s = 0
    while True:
        x = b[i]; i += 1
        r |= (x & 0x7f) << s
        if not (x & 0x80):
            break
        s += 7
    return r, i
i = 0; recs = []
while i < len(data):
    ln, i = rv(data, i)
    recs.append(data[i:i+ln]); i += ln
open("answer.txt", "wb").write(recs[2])
